stages.name: Data & Auth Export
stages.description: Export Firestore collections, Authentication users, and Storage buckets from Firebase Console or CLI.
steps: Run 'gcloud firestore export gs://[BUCKET_NAME]' to dump Firestore document trees.
Export Firebase Auth users via 'firebase auth:export users.json --format=json'.
Download Firebase Storage assets using 'gsutil -m cp -r gs://[PROJECT].appspot.com ./storage_backup'.
stages.tip: Firebase Auth password hashes use SCRYPT; Supabase Auth supports native scrypt hash migration.

stages.name: Host Environment Provisioning
stages.description: Spin up a dedicated Supabase instance locally or on a cloud VPS using Docker Compose.
steps: Clone or download the official Supabase Docker Compose definition.
Generate secure secrets for POSTGRES_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, and ANON_KEY.
Start all containers with 'docker compose up -d' and verify Studio UI on port 3000.
stages.tip: Ensure PostgreSQL port 5432 and Kong API Gateway port 8000 are accessible.

stages.name: Data Import & Schema Mapping
stages.description: Convert NoSQL document collections into relational PostgreSQL tables and import users.
steps: Create relational tables in PostgreSQL matching your Firestore collections (or use JSONB columns for flexible schemaless data).
Import user accounts into 'auth.users' table using the Supabase Firebase-Auth migration script.
Upload storage assets into Supabase Storage buckets via S3-compatible API.
stages.tip: Enable Row Level Security (RLS) on newly created tables to match Firebase Security Rules.

stages.name: Client SDK & API Cut-Over
stages.description: Replace Firebase Client SDK in your web or mobile frontend with @supabase/supabase-js.
steps: Install '@supabase/supabase-js' and replace firebase.initializeApp() with createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY).
Update authentication calls from signInWithEmailAndPassword to supabase.auth.signInWithPassword().
Switch real-time Firestore snapshots to supabase.channel().on('postgres_changes', ...).subscribe().
stages.tip: Deploy to a staging environment and test all auth, query, and subscription flows.

stages.name: Parity & Decommissioning Checklist
stages.description: Verify zero data loss and feature parity before canceling Firebase billing.
steps: Audit user sign-ins and session renewals on the new Supabase stack.
Run latency benchmarks comparing query response times.
Set Firebase project to read-only for 48 hours to catch any stranded clients.
Cancel paid Firebase Blaze plan to stop recurring monthly charges.
stages.tip: Keep the offline backup JSON archives stored safely for at least 90 days.

stages.name: Data & Collections Export
stages.description: Export Firestore collections as JSON files and download asset files.
steps: Export Firestore collections to JSON using firestore-export CLI tool.
Export user records from Firebase Auth console as CSV or JSON.

stages.name: PocketBase Binary Setup
stages.description: Run the single self-contained PocketBase Go binary on your machine or VPS.
steps: Download the PocketBase binary for your OS/Arch (Linux, macOS, Windows).
Start the server with './pocketbase serve --http="0.0.0.0:8090"'.
Navigate to 'http://localhost:8090/_/' and create your initial admin account.

stages.name: Collections Schema & Data Import
stages.description: Define collections in the Admin UI and bulk import JSON records.
steps: Create matching collections in PocketBase Admin UI with appropriate field types.
Run a quick Node.js script using 'pocketbase' SDK to batch-create records from exported JSON.

stages.name: Frontend SDK Cut-Over
stages.description: Install pocketbase SDK and update client authentication and queries.
steps: Install 'pocketbase' npm package in your application.
Initialize client: 'const pb = new PocketBase("http://127.0.0.1:8090")'.
Update auth and collection queries.

stages.name: Verification & Backup
stages.description: Enable automated SQLite backups and decommission Firebase.
steps: Configure automatic backup snapshots in PocketBase Settings > Backups.
Verify file upload and image thumbnails.
Downgrade/cancel Firebase Blaze billing.

stages.name: Export Postman Collection
stages.description: Export your Postman collections and environments to v2.1 JSON files.
steps: In Postman, click on your Collection's '...' menu and choose 'Export'.
Select 'Collection v2.1 (recommended)' and save the .json file locally.
Export your active Environment variables as JSON as well.

stages.name: Install Bruno Desktop
stages.description: Install Bruno native desktop app or CLI for your operating system.
steps: Download and install Bruno for macOS, Windows, or Linux.
Launch Bruno and choose a local directory on your disk where collection files will live.

stages.name: 1-Click Postman Import
stages.description: Import the exported Postman collection directly into plain Bru markup files.
steps: In Bruno home screen, click 'Import Collection'.
Select 'Postman Collection' and pick your exported .json file.
Select the destination folder on your machine where Bru files will be created.

stages.name: Git Repository Sync
stages.description: Commit your Bru files directly to your team's Git repository.
steps: Run 'git add . && git commit -m "chore: migrate API collection to Bruno"'.
Push to GitHub/GitLab. Now your API collection is versioned alongside your code!

stages.name: Run & Verify Requests
stages.description: Execute requests and verify environment variables.
steps: Run collection tests with Bruno CLI: 'bru run'.
Verify auth tokens and variables resolve properly.
Cancel Postman paid team seats.

stages.name: Export Password Vault
stages.description: Export your credentials as unencrypted CSV or JSON from your commercial password manager.
steps: In 1Password or Bitwarden, go to Settings > Export Vault.
Choose 'CSV' or 'JSON' format and save locally in a temporary directory.
Keep this file strictly confidential and delete immediately after import.

stages.name: Deploy Vaultwarden Container
stages.description: Spin up Vaultwarden using Docker with persistent storage and HTTPS.
steps: Start container: 'docker run -d --name vaultwarden -v /vw-data:/data -p 8088:80 --restart=always vaultwarden/server:latest'.
Configure SSL/TLS reverse proxy (Caddy or Nginx) since Bitwarden clients require HTTPS for WebCrypto APIs.

stages.name: Import Vault Data
stages.description: Create your master account in Vaultwarden Web Vault and import the file.
steps: Open your Vaultwarden URL and create your primary account with a strong master password.
Navigate to Tools > Import Data, select your export format, and upload the file.
Confirm all folders, logins, secure notes, and TOTP seeds imported cleanly.

stages.name: Connect Official Client Apps
stages.description: Point official Bitwarden browser extensions and mobile apps to your self-hosted server.
steps: In the Bitwarden extension or iOS/Android app, click the Gear icon on the login screen.
Enter your self-hosted Vaultwarden server URL in the 'Server URL' field.
Log in with your master credentials.

stages.name: Security Hardening & Cleanup
stages.description: Lock down signups, enable automated backup, and shred the plaintext export.
steps: Set environment variable 'SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false' to disable public registration.
Schedule daily backup of '/vw-data' folder to an encrypted offsite location.
Securely delete the unencrypted export CSV/JSON from your computer.
Cancel commercial password manager subscription.
